subject: Re: RAG evaluation — recommended models, reranker choice, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>, Priya Rao <priya@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap — RAG eval, recommended models, next steps

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and recommended path forward based on what you shared about ACME's internal KB and performance targets.

Call highlights:
- Goal: improve grounding accuracy for support answers while keeping median latency <= 400ms p95 for 1K token responses.
- Current infra: hybrid vector DB + S3-doc store, embedding model is a small on-host model with 768-d vectors.
- Primary risk: hallucination on long-tail KB entries and the cost sensitivity for high request volumes.

Recommended model & retrieval strategy (high-level):
1) Candidate model(s):
   - RW-7B-retrieval (quantized) — best cost/latency balance for high-throughput RAG.
   - Llama2-13B-instruct (float16) — better on abstractive answers when you need higher coherence; higher cost.
2) Embedding + retrieval:
   - Move to a 1024-d dense embedding for better semantic recall (we recommend the rw-embed-1k model).
   - Hybrid retrieval: dense ANN (Faiss/HNSW) + BM25 fallback. Settings to try: chunk_size=1000 tokens, chunk_overlap=128, top_k_retriever=50.
3) Reranker choice:
   - Cross-encoder reranker (rw-rerank-3b) as a second-stage reranker for top_k=50 -> rerank_top=5. This gives best grounding precision; expect added latency ~40-120ms depending on hardware.
   - If latency budget is tighter, use a lightweight cross-encoder or a learned bi-encoder comparator (lower cost, lower precision).
4) Grounding & QA metrics to track:
   - Source attribution rate (percentage of answers citing at least one doc).
   - Grounded-precision@k (manual eval suite).
   - Hallucination rate (manual labeling on sampling of responses).

Quality regression concerns and safeguards:
- We should run a small regression suite (we've started one for you) that includes: 150 prompt-q pairs across categories, several edge-case queries, and a confusion matrix for reranker vs retriever-only answers.
- Canary rollouts: A/B deploy RW-7B-retrieval vs Llama2-13B-instruct on 10% traffic with strict SLA checks for latency and grounding metrics.

Deliverables I can share (attached / linked):
- ACME_RAG_prompt_set_v2.txt — prompt templates and test prompts we discussed.
- acme_rag_benchmarks_20260225.xlsx — benchmark spreadsheet (starter results + suggested experiments).
- sample_reranker_latency_report.pdf — sample numbers from a similar customer.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll share the sample prompt set + benchmark sheet (attached).
2) Your team to share a subset of 1K representative docs (or a snapshot export) so we can run a baseline retrieval experiment.
3) Schedule a 45-min technical review + demo with Dylan (serving/runtime) to discuss deployment & estimated cost.
4) We will propose an initial mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and success criteria.

Would you be available for the technical review next week (Mar 3 or Mar 4)? I’ve cc'd Monica to help with scheduling and the MAP.

Best,
Marissa

Great — thanks Jordan. Quick answers inline, plus next steps and links.

1) Reranker latency & cost:
   - If the reranker runs on a dedicated GPU (A10/A100 class), expect an additional 40-120ms p50/p95 per request for a 3B cross-encoder. Cost depends on throughput and reserved capacity; for your traffic profile our initial estimate is roughly $0.004–$0.012 per request on top of base generation/embedding costs (will refine after we run a baseline).

2) Example prompt templates (excerpt from attached prompt set):
   - System: "You are an internal support assistant. Always cite the source document (title and section) when the answer references internal content. If you are unsure, respond with "I don't know; please check the following documents:" followed by suggested sources."
   - User: "Customer: [customer_question]"
   - Instruction: "Return a concise answer (<=120 words), bullet list of steps if action is required, and a sources block with up to 3 cited docs and excerpts."

3) Snapshot format: JSONL with fields {id, text, title, metadata}. Redact PII fields and replace with <REDACTED>. Please include source timestamps where available.

Next steps (I’ll take these actions):
- I’ve uploaded the prompt set + benchmark sheet to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeRAGBenchmarks
- Dylan will join the technical review on Mar 3 10am PT (invite sent).
- Monica will draft a short MAP and success criteria template and share it by EOD Tue; initial MAP will include: baseline retrieval eval, reranker A/B, canary rollout, and SLA checks.
- We’ll run a baseline retrieval experiment once you share the 1K doc snapshot (sample run ~48 hours).

Attachments & quick links: ACME_RAG_prompt_set_v2.txt (attached), acme_rag_benchmarks_20260225.xlsx (attached), sample_reranker_latency_report.pdf (attached).
